name: fixed-alloc
algorithm: Per iteration, two 8-byte objects are allocated from a fixed-buffer allocator over a 64 KiB stack buffer through the standard allocator interface, read, and freed in LIFO order, so each request reaches the allocator's alloc and free; the checksum folds the values (../README.md).

skip.c: no fixed-buffer allocator in the C standard library
skip.rust: no fixed-buffer allocator in Rust's standard library (the Allocator API is unstable)
skip.go: no fixed-buffer allocator in Go's standard library

notes: Mk: std.mem.Fixed with Box[u64].New and Take; Zig: std.heap.FixedBufferAllocator with Allocator.create and destroy.
